0.1 This

FOREWORD

Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Indian 1985, after the draft finalized by the LaboraInstitution on 30 October toryware and Related Apparatus Sectional Committee had been approved by the Chemical Division Council. 0.2 This standard covers the methods of test which are intended to give an assessment of the chemical resistance of colour marking colour coded according to enamels used on laboratory glasssware Detergent and acid solutions have been chosen to IS : 11468- 1985*. represent the most servere conditions to be encountered in practice. 0.3 In the formulation of this standard considerable assistance has been taken from IS0 4794-1982 `Laboratory.glassware methods for chemical resistance of enamels used for colour codmg and colour marking', issued by the International Organization for Standardization ( IS0 ), Geneva. 0.4 In reporting the result of a test or analysis made in accordance with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS : 2-19607.

.

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard specifies test methods for the assessment of the service performance of enamels used for colour coding and colour marking of It does not purport to classify enamels by their laboratory glassware. degree of resistance; it provides standard procedures for determining whether an enamel resists the specified treatment without a change such that the colour can no longer be identified, or might be confused with any other colour used in colour coding.

IS : 11469 - 1985 1.1.1 The procedures involve treatment for specified periods with an alkaline detergent solution at 80�C and a dilute acid solution at room temperature. 2. PREPARATION OF TEST PIECES

2.1 Cut test pieces from the laboratory glassware so as to include the complete colour marking enamel to be assessed plus at least 5 mm of the Wash each test piece three times in adjacent parts of the glassware. separate portions of the cold water and wipe with the cleaning cloth, then wash three times in separate portions of the cold acetone. Finally, wipe the test pieces with the cleaning cloth to remove all traces of soiling, and transfer them to a stoppered storage vessel, unless proceed immediately with testing. 3. Procedure

3.2.3.1 Transfer about 700 ml of the cold hydrochloric acid to the beaker and allow to stand until it reaches room temperature.

Suspend not more than 10 test pieces, with the aid of the sample holder in the hydrochloric acid so that the test pieces are freely in contact with the acid on all sides, and cover with the beaker cover glass. Allow to stand for 60 f 5 min at room temperature. After this period, remove the test pieces from the acid, wash them thoroughly with water, wipe with the cleaning cloth and then rinse three times in fresh portions of acetone. Allow to drain dry. 4. INTERPRETATION

OF RESULTS

4.1 At the end of each test, compare the colour of the enamel on each of the test pieces with that of a similar test piece which has been prepared in accordance with 2 and then store without further treatment.

IS: 11469 - 1985

1

Disregard any loss of gloss in the treatment test pieces, but note any change or loss of colour such as might lead to the loss of colour marking or to confusion with any other colour used in colour coding. 4.2 Resistance to Detergent Solutions

4.2.1 A colour coding enamel, when prepared in accordance with 2 and tested as specified in 3.1, is regarded as passing the test, if it does not change in colour, with or without loss of gloss, to the extent that its identity is lost or that it can be confused with any other colour used for colour coding. 4.3 Resistance to Acid Solutions

4.3.1 A colour coding enamel, when prepared in accordance with 2 and tested as specified in 3.2, is regarded as passing the test `if it does not change in colour, with or without loss of gloss, to the extent that its identity is lost or that it can be confused with any other colour used for colour coding. 4.4 Conditions for Re-test

4.4.1 If in either test for the resistance to detergent solutions or the test for resistance to acid solutions, any of the test pieces has changed colour to an unacceptable extent, then test shall be repeated with a fresh sample of the colour which failed. No failures on re-test are permitted. 5. TEST 5.1 The REPORT following minimum description from which information shall be given in test report: of laboratory
